page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. One marginal note in the left margin, beside the paragraph beginning "5. Modi". Page number and running head at the top.

main_text.p: Fuit autem in illis, 1. προηγούμενον[?]. Calamitas praesupponit culpam. Item, Saepe fit, ut ob unius noxam multi laborent.
2. [illegible, ~12 letters], Tempestas praesentem intentans omnibus mortem.
3. Finis proximus, Rei hominis agnitio: superior, eiusdem iusta poena: summus, incolumitas, qua se, nocente praesente, nec poenis affecto, potiri non posse, iudicabant.
Forma.5. Modi deprehendendi fontes, multiplices sunt. Hoc loco fortis mentio fit, de qua paulo post dicam.

Olim fontes deprehendebatur per applicationem tribuum, familiarum, personarum. Iof. 7. Ac sunt, qui Arcam & pe-storale (in quo erat Urim & Thumim) adhibita fuisse dicant. Eodem fecit, Aqua zelotypiae, Sors, & alia quaedam.
Cum mirabdis modis hominum occulta mala Deus retegat, studendum est ve-rae pietati, & orandus Dominus, ut ne patiatur nos labi in tetros furores & errores.
6. Nec est cur filij Dei putent, occultanda esse sua ἁμαρτήματα, caeterorum aut hominum errata & peccata retegeda. Nam quo maiora in illos, quam in hosce, χαρίσ-ματα[?]

page.notes: Greek item 1 ("προηγούμενον") and the Greek word after "hosce" ("χαρίσ-ματα") are uncertain; the Greek word in item 2 is not legible letter by letter. "pe-storale" is read with uncertainty in the printed word; "orandus" appears as "orădus" in the print. "praesente" may be printed with a ę ligature. The Latin "Iof. 7." is kept as printed. The printed "Vrim" was corrected to "Urim" under the u/v rule, and "vierunt" to "vierunt" with consonant v; check the first word. Rule 1: spellings such as "Cùm", "Eôdem" were normalised for accents only where the accent is a grave or circumflex mark over a letter.
